root_cause_criterion.function: pcpp::BgpLayer::parseBgpLayer(unsigned char*, unsigned long, pcpp::Layer*, pcpp::Packet*)
root_cause_criterion.criterion: Before `parseBgpLayer()` materializes a BGP UPDATE as `BgpUpdateMessageLayer`, the bytes needed to reach the path-attributes-length field must fit inside `dataLen`.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable parser instantiates the malformed terminal UPDATE even though its withdrawn-routes field pushes the path-attributes-length field beyond the available message bytes. The fixed parser adds UPDATE-specific validation at the same admission site.

nodes.description: After the helper restores the original withdrawn-routes vector on the malformed terminal UPDATE, that UPDATE remains only 21 bytes long, below the 23-byte minimum assumed by the NLRI setter.
The vulnerable NLRI setter still requests insertion at fixed offset 23 even though the current terminal UPDATE is shorter than that offset.

nodes.function: pcpp::RawPacket::insertData(int, unsigned char const*, unsigned long)
nodes.description: At the raw-packet insertion sink, the computed insertion index `atIndex` is already past the current packet end `m_RawDataLen`, so the subsequent `memmove()` length becomes negative.

edges.from_function: pcpp::BgpLayer::parseBgpLayer(unsigned char*, unsigned long, pcpp::Layer*, pcpp::Packet*)
edges.description: The exact `BgpUpdateMessageLayer*` object materialized for the terminal malformed UPDATE is the object whose header has collapsed below the NLRI minimum by the time the helper finishes restoring withdrawn routes.
The same post-restore header length remains in force when `setNetworkLayerReachabilityInfo()` chooses its insertion offset.
The fixed layer-relative insertion offset chosen by `setNetworkLayerReachabilityInfo()` is passed unchanged into `Packet::extendLayer()` as `offsetInLayer`.

edges.to_function: pcpp::RawPacket::insertData(int, unsigned char const*, unsigned long)
edges.description: The packet-relative insertion index computed in `Packet::extendLayer()` is passed unchanged to `RawPacket::insertData()` as `atIndex`.
